Build an Oblique Random-Forest Learner Adapter (Experimental)

make_aorsf_adapter.Rd

Experimental learner adapter extending STABL to non-linear signals with oblique random forests (aorsf). One forest is fit per bootstrap subsample; the "penalty path" is an importance-threshold path built from quantiles of the pooled negation-importance distribution (see auto_oblique_threshold_grid()), so the selection set grows monotonically as the threshold decreases — the same sparse-to-dense nesting the lambda path provides for glmnet learners.

Usage

make_aorsf_adapter(num_trees = 500L)

Arguments

num_trees

Positive integer; number of trees per aorsf oblique forest.

Value

A function with signature function(x, y, lambda_val) -> logical vector of length ncol(x), mirroring make_glmnet_adapter(): the mask selects features whose negation importance meets the threshold carried by lambda_val.

Details

Experimental: this is a stablr extension beyond Python STABL, and FDP+ calibration for oblique random-forest learners is empirical (validated separately by the F5 benchmark), not a theoretical guarantee.

Statistical guardrails: negation importance is used (not permutation importance) because it discriminates relevant from irrelevant predictors better in oblique forests (Jaeger et al. 2023). Oblique random forests must be paired with model-X knockoff artificial features (knockoff_equi / knockoff_mvr): permuted nulls do not receive the correlation leakage that real null features receive in a multivariate learner, so random_permutation nulls make FDP+ anti-conservative — stablr warns when this combination is requested.

D2 caveat: importance is spread across the linear combinations used in each split, so per-feature selection frequencies are noisier than for axis-aligned random forests (make_ranger_adapter()); small stability-score differences between features are less reliable and more bootstraps are recommended.

See also

auto_oblique_threshold_grid(), make_ranger_adapter(), make_glmnet_adapter(), stabl_fit() (base_learner = "oblique_rf").

Examples

if (requireNamespace("aorsf", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1L)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 6), 60, 6,
              dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:60), paste0("f", 1:6)))
  y <- setNames(0.8 * x[, 1] + 0.8 * x[, 2] + 0.5 * x[, 1] * x[, 2] +
                rnorm(60, sd = 0.3), rownames(x))
  adapter <- make_aorsf_adapter(num_trees = 100L)
  grid <- auto_oblique_threshold_grid(x, y, n_grid = 5L, num_trees = 100L, seed = 1L)
  mask <- adapter(x, y, grid[1L, ])  # sparsest end of the path
  cat("selected:", sum(mask), "of", ncol(x), "features\n")
}
#> selected: 1 of 6 features
